# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which states that the yellow wire must be cut when the light is orange, and that the light cycles through three colours every round. 

However, as the Mute monkey, I cannot speak—I can only gesture to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures, and Deaf cannot hear speech. Deaf has not yet seen the bomb or spoken to establish any shared code or vocabulary for gestures ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Furthermore, I do not yet know the layout of the wires or the sequence of light colours that Deaf can see, nor do I know what Blind can feel on the bomb.

Before sending any signals, I must wait for Blind and Deaf to speak in Round 1 so that the state of the bomb is described and a mutual understanding or convention can be formed.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can only hear speech and cut wires. Since you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak it aloud to me.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is orange. WIRES: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue. Mute, read the manual and gesture the instruction to me; I will speak it aloud to Blind. Use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or other clear hand signs.

I have read the defusal manual. It specifies:
- The light changes every round in a circle of three colours.
- What matters is what the light shows at the moment of the cut.
- To defuse, we must cut the yellow wire (wire 2) specifically when the light is orange.

In Round 1, Deaf observed that the light was orange. Since the light changes every round through a cycle of three colours, it will not be orange in Round 2 or Round 3; it will return to orange in Round 4.

If I signal wire 2 (`✌`) right now in Round 2, Deaf will immediately relay the cut command to Blind, and Blind will cut wire 2 in Round 3 while the light is not orange, detonating the bomb.

Therefore, we must hold. Deaf asked for ☝, ✌, 🤟, or "other clear hand signs." I will gesture ✋ (stop / wait) to Deaf so Deaf knows not to cut yet and to inform Blind to hold, allowing Deaf to notice the light cycle and coordinate timing.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The LIGHT turned green! DISPLAY is still 0. Wires are still intact: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured ✋ (hand / stop / five). Mute, is the bomb defused? Gesture 👍 if solved, or gesture specific instructions if more steps remain.

I need Deaf to instruct Blind to cut wire 2 (the yellow wire).

The manual states:
- The light walks the same circle of three colours every round.
- It was orange in Round 1, green in Round 2, which means it will be the third colour in Round 3, and return to orange in Round 4.
- In each round, the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf.
- When I gesture wire 2 (`✌`) now in Round 3, Deaf will receive it at the end of Round 3 and speak to Blind. Blind will receive Deaf's instruction at the beginning of Round 4.
- When Blind cuts wire 2 during Round 4, the light will have cycled back to orange, satisfying the defusal condition.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The LIGHT has turned RED. Mute gestured ✌ (two fingers). Blind, cut wire 2 (the yellow wire / second wire)!

I have already conveyed the target wire (wire 2, yellow) to Deaf, who has instructed Blind to cut wire 2. 

The light cycle was orange in Round 1, green in Round 2, and red in Round 3. Now in Round 4, the light returns to orange. Blind acts immediately after me in this round and has Deaf's instruction to cut wire 2 (yellow) during this turn, which perfectly satisfies the defusal manual's condition. No further gestures are needed from me.

```
wait()
```
